subject: POC priming: sandbox key sync, VPC allowlist & demo runbook
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC priming: sandbox key sync, VPC allowlist & demo runbook

Hi Rajiv —

Excited to get the POC scheduled. Before we lock a hands-on session, a quick checklist so the kickoff is smooth:

- Confirm a 90-minute working session slot (we suggest 60 min hands-on + 30 min load/scaling checks).
- Sandbox API keys: we will provide short-lived keys scoped to the staging project. Please confirm the email for provisioning and whether you need cross-account role access.
- VPC/IP allowlist: we need the egress IP range for your staging environment and can provide our public egress range for allowlisting.
- Routing & endpoints: do you want to test with our default staging endpoints or a custom VPC endpoint?
- Load window: propose a 30m load test, non-business-hours preferred (we can run in the evening).

I've attached a lightweight runbook and an allowlist CSV template to speed the network ops work. Ben will cover prompt review during the session — he can tailor a short prompt pack if you share the top-3 production intents you want to validate.

Proposed kickoff slots (PDT):
- Tue, Apr 20 10:00–11:30
- Wed, Apr 21 14:00–15:30
- Thu, Apr 22 17:30–19:00 (after-hours load window)

Can you confirm which slot works and the contact for your network/security engineer?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-poc-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook, 4 pages); vpc-allowlist-template.csv (CSV)

From: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@lumenhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumen Health EngOps <engops@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC priming: sandbox key sync, VPC allowlist & demo runbook

Irene —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Wed, Apr 21 14:00–15:30 PDT works best for our team. I'll loop in our cloud engineer (cc: engops).

A few quick notes from our side:
- Sandbox keys: provision to rajiv.patel@lumenhealth.com and scope to read/write only in the "lh-staging-redwood" project.
- VPC allowlist: we'll need your egress IP ranges and the TLS fingerprint if possible. We prefer to terminate within our VPC (private endpoint) for the POC — is that supported for staging?
- Load test: we'll take the 30m evening window; can you propose an after-hours slot if we want to avoid spoiling daytime latency metrics?

Also, procurement asked if there will be any data retention on your side during the POC (short answer is OK) so they can sign off quickly.

Rajiv
Senior Eng Manager, Lumen Health
rpatel@lumenhealth.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC priming: sandbox key sync, VPC allowlist & demo runbook

Rajiv —

Great — locking Wed, Apr 21 14:00–15:30 PDT for the working session. Calendar invite incoming from Aditya.

Answers inline:
- Sandbox keys: we'll create two short-lived API keys (one for your app team, one for your QA engineer). Keys will be scoped to "lh-staging-redwood" with token TTL=12 hours by default. Please confirm the two provisioning emails (rajiv.patel@lumenhealth.com plus the QA contact).
- Private endpoint: yes, we support a private VPC endpoint for Redwood Private customers; for Hosted POC we can provide a temporary private endpoint via our partner VPC peering workflow. To proceed we'll need: your VPC ID, region, and a CIDR range for the peering connection. If peering isn't possible we'll fall back to allowlisting our public egress.
- Egress IPs & TLS: attached is the egress IP list (same CSV). We can't share private TLS fingerprints for hosted endpoints, but if you host the endpoint in your VPC we'll provide a self-signed cert for the test.
- Data retention: no long-term retention — POC logs retained for 7 days by default and are purged unless you request an export. We'll include standard POC terms in the runbook.

Action items for Lumen ops (please reply here):
1) Confirm QA provisioning email for second key.
2) Share VPC ID + region if you want the private endpoint (or reply "allowlist" to use public egress).
3) Confirm after-hours load window preference (Wed 20:00–20:30 PDT or Thu 19:00–19:30 PDT).

Ben — when you have the prompt intents, drop them here and I'll pre-seed a short prompt pack. Tessa will prepare a short failure/fallback checklist for the load test.

Thanks,
Irene

From: Lumen Health EngOps <engops@lumenhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC priming: sandbox key sync, VPC allowlist & demo runbook

Irene / Aditya —

Thanks. QA contact is mimisha.desai@lumenhealth.com. For the private endpoint we'd like to try peering; VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d, region: us-west-2. CIDR for peering: 10.200.0.0/16.

We prefer Wed evening for the load window — Wed 20:00–20:30 PDT is good. We will need the egress ranges now so security can stamp the change; the allowlist CSV you attached was helpful. Please confirm a single contact we can ping during the window for immediate rollback.

Also: procurement asked for the POC data retention statement in writing for their ticket — see snippet below and please confirm: "Redwood retains transient logs for test traffic for up to 7 days and does not persist PII beyond troubleshooting windows unless explicitly requested."

—EngOps (on behalf of Lumen Health)
